articles.title: College Hockey Coach Emily McNamara Dead at 42 Months After Being Involved in Car Accident
articles.summary: Middlebury College assistant women’s hockey coach Emily McNamara has died, months after being involved in a major car accident near the school’s Vermont camp...
articles.body:
Middlebury College assistant women's hockey coach Emily McNamara has died , months after being involved in a major car accident near the school's Vermont campus. She was 42.

A Middlebury alum, McNamara returned to her alma mater in 2023 to help coach the team she once played for. She previously served as head coach at Hamilton College. Her cause of death has not been revealed.

"With deep sadness, we share the news that Assistant Women's Ice Hockey Coach Emily McNamara '07 died on Friday, September 11," Middlebury President Ian Baucom said in a statement shared via Instagram on Sunday, September 13. "As many of you know, Emily suffered serious injuries in a car accident last winter."

The statement continued, "We have been in touch with Emily's family to share our sorrow and our full support during this difficult time. We have also spoken with members of our women's hockey team and Athletics staff, who are understandably heartbroken by this news. Emily's husband Dave , all her family, her colleagues, the students on the team, and everyone who knew her are deeply in our hearts."

McNamara was critically injured on March 20 when an ice storm caused her car to lose traction and collide with a tractor trailer driving in the opposite direction. Her life-threatening injuries included multiple fractures to her face, neck, clavicle, ribs and pelvis, as well as a traumatic brain injury, according to a GoFundMe page set up to cover her medical bills.

In the months that followed, McNamara underwent multiple surgeries and spent time on a ventilator while she was unable to breathe on her own. By late April, she was well enough to be transferred to a rehabilitation center where she continued her recovery, participating in physical and occupational therapy, as well as speech and language pathology sessions.

In July, McNamara was able to move into her family's home in New Hampshire, where she continued to receive care through in-home nursing and therapy services.

Hamilton College also shared a statement on social media, remembering McNamara as more than just a coach.

"She was the person who answered the phone at midnight for a player going through something hard," the statement read. "She was the coach who remembered every player's family, every player's story, long after they graduated. She was, to two generations of Hamilton and Middlebury hockey players, someone who believed in them before they believed in themselves."

The statement continued, "Hamilton Athletics extends its deepest condolences to Dave, to the McNamara family, and to everyone at Middlebury College who loved and worked alongside Coach Mac. Her impact on this program, on this conference, and on the sport of women's hockey will not be forgotten."

articles.title: Leslie Romero bate el récord de España de velocidad y roza una histórica medalla en Chongqing
articles.standfirst: Acaba cuarta en las Speed World Climbing Series de la localidad china, su mejor puesto
articles.summary: Acaba cuarta en las Speed World Climbing Series de la localidad china, su mejor puesto
articles.body: Leslie Romero ha vuelto a demostrar que se ha instalado definitivamente en la élite mundial con un nuevo récord de España y un histórico cuarto puesto en las World Series de velocidad en Chongqing (China). La escaladora nacida en Venezuela pero afincada en España ha firmado un tiempo de 6.257 segundos en su tercera manga (carril C), acabando segunda en la general de las clasificatorias, únicamente por detrás de la estadounidense Emma Hunt (6.093). Carla Martínez Vidal también certificó su billete a la fase de eliminación directa al clasificarse en 13.ª posición, con un mejor tiempo de 6.686 segundos, consolidando la progresión de la escalada de velocidad española en la élite mundial. Ya en la fase de eliminación directa, Carla superó los octavos antes de caer en cuartos mientras que Leslie avanzó hasta la ronda final, cayendo en la lucha por el bronce (8.04) frente a la italiana Giulia Randi (6.53). En la batalla por el oro, Hunt (6.13) confirmó su mejor tiempo de las clasificatorias venciendo a la china shaoqin Zhang (6.30). En categoría masculina, ni Miguel Gómez, 35º con 5.167 segundos, ni Erik Noya, 37º con 5.292, avanzaron a fase de eliminación directa.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Week 2 lineup picks from Justin Boone
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Justin Boone reveals his lineup tips for Week 2.
articles.body:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 2 rankings .

After a surprising upset loss to the Giants and a subdued stat line from Prescott, the Cowboys head home to Dallas for a get-right game against the Commanders.

Washington just allowed a three-touchdown day to Jalen Hurts and remains a matchup to target. Prescott topped 22 fantasy points against the Commanders in both their meetings last year, finishing as a top-10 QB on both occasions.

The Cowboys defense still looks like a work in progress, so you can expect plenty of fireworks in a contest with the second-highest projected point total on the week (50.5).

Brock Purdy vs. Dolphins – Purdy has quickly become one of the most consistent fantasy quarterbacks. If he was able to throw for three touchdowns when facing the Rams, there should be no issues against a Dolphins defense that just let Kirk Cousins toss three scores.

Jaxson Dart at LAR – Dart picked up where he left off last season, making plays through the air and on the ground. His rushing upside alone makes him a weekly fantasy starter and the matchup is far less concerning against a Rams defense returning from Australia with Myles Garrett now on injured reserve.

A thumb injury has landed Jordan Mason on IR, paving the way for Jones to jump back into the fantasy RB2 mix.

In his four starts against the Bears since arriving in Minnesota , Jones has averaged 96 scrimmage yards per game and scored three touchdowns against them. We also just watched another veteran back, Chuba Hubbard , put up 87 yards and two TDs on Chicago last week.

With rookie Demond Claiborne still getting acclimated to the NFL and DeeJay Dallas being more of a special-teams asset, Jones is a strong start this week.

Javonte Williams vs. Commanders – Williams has very little competition for touches in what's projected to be a high-scoring outing where the Cowboys are favored. He scored touchdowns in both appearances against Washington last season and I expect him to find the end zone once again.

Bucky Irving vs. Browns – Despite the addition of Kenneth Gainwell this offseason, Irving dominated the Buccaneers backfield work in Week 1. He's positioned for another big day as a mid-range fantasy RB2 with RB1 upside as the Bucs are eight-point favorites at home.

Chuba Hubbard at Falcons – While Jonathon Brooks will likely earn an increased role as the season goes along, Hubbard dominated the backfield with a 71% snap share. This is a positive matchup for the Panthers versus a Falcons team that is struggling to find competent quarterback play.

After finishing as the WR16 in fantasy points per game last year during his 10 outings, Watson took his game to yet another tier in Week 1 with six catches, 147 yards and two scores.

While we can't expect him to be the second-highest scoring fantasy wideout every week, that's the kind of ceiling Watson offers thanks to his big-play ability — even against a tougher opponent like the Vikings.

The degree of difficulty won't be nearly as challenging versus the Jets, who were barely tested by the Titans ' passing attack last week. Watson is flirting with low-end WR1 status in this matchup.

Mike Evans vs. Dolphins – De'Zhaun Stribling on IR, George Kittle still rounding into form and the 49ers still projected for the second-most points on the week. I'll be shocked if Evans doesn't come down with at least one of the scores in this spot.

Garrett Wilson vs. Packers – Wilson may not have found the end zone last week, but his 6-79-0 stat line was a positive indicator of things to come. Green Bay 's secondary is a major weakness and one he can exploit, just like Justin Jefferson did en route to a two-TD performance in Week 1.

Tetairoa McMillan /Jalen Coker at Falcons – After a solid Week 1 from McMillan (75 yards) and a monster performance from Coker (138 yards, two TDs) the Panthers should feast again in Atlanta . McMillan's best outing as a rookie (130 yards, two TDs) came against the Falcons in Week 11.

Zay Flowers is dealing with a hamstring injury that will likely sideline him in Week 2. Rising rookie Ja'Kobi Lane is on IR after undergoing wrist surgery. Rashod Bateman has never proven himself as a consistent threat and the depth chart behind him is filled with role players.

That points to a more old-school approach from the Ravens offense, which will need to lean on Lamar Jackson , Derrick Henry and Andrews against the Saints.

In his first game under promising new OC Declan Doyle, Andrews posted six catches and 49 yards. Those totals would have been his second-highest marks all of last season. He's a strong volume-based TE1 this week.

Dalton Schultz vs. Bengals – With Nico Collins expected to miss Week 2 and Jayden Higgins out for the season, the Texans have no choice but to rely on their veteran tight end. He's another volume-based low-end TE1.

Hunter Henry vs. Steelers – Are you sensing a theme? The Patriots also lost their top receiver A.J. Brown to injury, which vaults Henry back into the fantasy streamer conversation. His best performance of 2025 came against the Steelers (8-90-2). He also had a decent outing against their new DC Patrick Graham (4-66-0) when he was with the Raiders.

Whenever you have a quarterback of Burrow's caliber with weapons like Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown , it's hard to recommend sitting them in fantasy. Burrow is often matchup-proof, but there are a few reasons why you may want to consider another option this week.

The first is a back issue that's led to two straight limited practices. While it's possible Burrow is just taking it easy and will be fine for Sunday (he said he would play), we know back problems can be sporadic and impact a quarterback's accuracy.

We also have the matchup with the Texans to consider. Though Josh Allen was able to carve them up, there are no guarantees a less-than-100% Burrow will have the same success versus one of the better defenses in the league. I'm treating Burrow as a volatile high-end fantasy QB2 this week.

Malik Willis at 49ers – Willis' rushing stats will always keep him in the fantasy streamer mix, but I'm not risking him in my lineup on a cross-country trip to battle a 49ers defense that looked ferocious in the opener.

C.J. Stroud vs. Bengals – If Collins doesn't suit up, it's impossible to use Stroud as anything other than a desperation low-end QB2 in Superflex leagues.

Judkins occupied this space last week due to a tough matchup with the Jaguars and the result was 12 carries for 33 rushing yards, two receptions for 17 yards and an RB39 fantasy finish.

Better days will come for the talented sophomore, but it likely won't be as part of eight-point road dogs against the Buccaneers. Vita Vea and the Bucs front has historically been tough sledding for running backs and Judkins' limited role in the passing game is a problem.

When Dylan Sampson went down, third-stringer Raheim Sanders stepped into his role. It's possible Judkins will earn more work in the receiving game moving forward, but I'm not banking on that this week. He's once again a TD-or-bust RB3 for fantasy.

J.K. Dobbins vs. Jaguars – The Jaguars are a shutdown unit against opposing rushing attacks and Dobbins is on a short week after putting up just 36 yards against the Chiefs on Monday.

Tony Pollard vs. Eagles – Pollard only managed 35 yards on seven carries versus the Jets last week. It's not even the near 50-50 split with Tyjae Spears that scares me. I'm more worried about the state of the Titans offense and their awful blocking. A matchup with the Eagles isn't going to help.

Rico Dowdle at Patriots – Despite leading the backfield in snaps last week, Dowdle only produced 21 yards on his 10 touches. New England boasts a quality run defense that will be focused on shutting down the Steelers' backs.

The Falcons' quarterback situation is absolutely tanking London's fantasy value early in the season. With Tua Tagovailoa suffering from an oblique injury, Atlanta hasn't had a bridge quarterback to cover until Michael Penix Jr. is fully recovered from his ACL tear.

Penix practiced in full last week before being ruled out and, according to reports , that's the most likely scenario for Sunday. Though Penix has split first-team reps with Cooper Rush , it's Rush who's expected to get another start.

That is disastrous for London, who managed just two catches for 29 yards on five targets in the opener. Once Penix returns, London will go back to being a potential fantasy WR1 like we saw last season, when he finished as the WR7 in fppg and was the third-highest scoring wideout through the first 11 weeks before injuries struck. However, until Penix starts, London is down in the fantasy WR3 range.

Marvin Harrison Jr. vs. Seahawks – After being out-targeted by Trey McBride , Michael Wilson and even Kendrick Bourne in Week 1, we need to see something from Harrison before we trust him in our lineups.

Jayden Reed at Jets – The hope that the Packers would use more three-receiver sets and make Reed something closer to a full-time player didn't materialize in Week 1. Instead, he played just 57% of the snaps and only came away with three catches for 20 yards. He's a WR4/flex at best right now, with Christian Watson and Matthew Golden being the Packers wideouts you want to roster.

Carnell Tate/Wan'Dale Robinson vs. Eagles – The Titans offense looks like the worst in the league at the moment. While we can give them a bit of grace as they get comfortable in Brian Daboll's scheme, there aren't a lot of signs that this is going to improve anytime soon.

The Browns drafting two receivers early was always a concern for Fannin's target share and we saw that come to fruition in Week 1.

Fannin earned just three targets, fewer than wideouts Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion Jr. and Jerry Jeudy . It's particularly discouraging since the Browns were trailing all afternoon, something they project to do often this year.

Fannin will still have some strong outings in 2026, but averaging nearly seven targets per contest like he did as a rookie seems unlikely. That bumps him down to low-end TE1 territory.

Kyle Pitts Sr. vs. Panthers – Pitts is in a similar situation as Drake London. He will be hard to trust in your lineup until Michael Penix Jr. gets back under center. He also hasn't topped 40 yards in any of his last three outings versus the Panthers.

Jake Ferguson vs. Commanders – Ferguson is trapped behind CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy in the Cowboys' passing attack. That turns him into a TD-or-bust TE2. You can find a streamer with more projected volume.

articles.title: English soccer club sorry for launching ‘United 93’ clothing collection around 9/11 anniversary
articles.summary: English soccer club Oxford United has apologized for releasing US-style apparel with “United 93” on the back around the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks, saying the clothing range was launched “without understanding of the historical context and associations.”
articles.body: English soccer club Oxford United has apologized for releasing US-style apparel with “United 93” on the back around the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks, saying the clothing range was launched “without understanding of the historical context and associations.” The team, which plays in England’s third tier, said Friday it has removed the collection with immediate effect and was reviewing its approval processes. Oxford United was founded in 1893, initially as Headington FC before a name change in 1960. United Airlines Flight 93 was one of the four planes hijacked on September 11, 2001, during the attacks that brought down the World Trade Center’s twin towers and blew a hole in the Pentagon. The plane was headed for Washington, officials have concluded, but the aircraft went down in Pennsylvania after passengers and crew members stormed the cockpit and fought the hijackers. In a club statement, Oxford United said it wanted to “sincerely apologize” for the launch of its Campus Collection, which, according to local media, featured an American football jersey and a baseball jersey. “The range was released without understanding of the historical context and associations,” the statement read. “It should not have reached the point of sale and we take full responsibility for not undertaking proper due diligence. “We have removed the collection with immediate effect and are reviewing our approval processes to ensure nothing like this happens again.” The page announcing the launch of the Campus Collection has been deleted.

articles.title: Hibs: 'Living legend' Gray can be proud of record, says Newell
articles.summary: Club captain Joe Newell insists sacked head coach David Gray can be proud of his record at Hibernian and believes his replacement has plenty of time to deliver success this season.
articles.body:
Club captain Joe Newell insists sacked head coach David Gray can be proud of his record at Hibernian and believes his replacement has plenty of time to deliver success this season.

Gray's 12-year stay at Easter Road came to an end on Wednesday, with Hibs on a run of three successive Scottish Premiership defeats and ninth in the table after six games.

"It's been a tough week for everyone," said 33-year-old midfielder Newell, who was a team-mate of Gray's when he signed in 2019 and who was made skipper when the former boss took charge.

"There's an element of blame for all of us. He always took responsibility, always protected his players, which I thought was noble and kind of summed him up as a man.

"Football moves on quickly, but I think it's important everyone at the club remembers him for what he's done - and I'm sure they will. He's not just a living legend. He'll go down in history."

Gray captained Hibs to Scottish Cup glory in 2016, famously scoring a stoppage-time winner against Rangers in the final at Hampden.

As a rookie head coach, he led the Edinburgh side to third and fifth-place finishes.

"His time in charge of the club was a massive success," Newell said. "The more time goes on, the more people will appreciate that.

"From the place we were in to where we went under Dave is something he should be proud of.

"We've had some amazing memories over the last couple of years and some really good achievements."

Painful endgame for Gray as stale Hibs slump

Gray sacked by Hibs after six league games

Hibs face Aberdeen on Saturday hoping to avoid what would be a club record of seven successive home league defeats.

"The main thing is the reaction, to try and get back on winning terms with a performance the fans can get behind," Newell said.

Hibs will meet city rivals Heart of Midlothian in the Premier Sports Cup semi-finals on 1 November and Newell is sure this campaign can be a fruitful one.

"All we can do as players is buy into whoever is in charge," he added.

"There's no crisis in terms of saving the season. It's still early on. We are in a position where we can turn it round quickly.

"I've said it a few times on record that this squad, and especially over the last 12 months, is the best squad I've been involved in, so I'm massively confident that we can still achieve what we've set out to achieve."

articles.title: Bold Fantasy Football Predictions for Week 2
articles.summary: It's time to get bold for fantasy football in Week 2.
articles.body:
The Yahoo Fantasy Football crew is ready to get bold for Week 2. Which one of these predictions will come true?

Uncs Stefon Diggs , Deebo Samuel Sr. finish as top-30 WRs

Diggs, nearly 33 years old, and Samuel, 30 (but a lot older in football years), had excellent debuts in terms of their involvement on new teams. Diggs had four grabs directly on elite slot CB Cooper DeJean and was moved across the formation as their primary schemed up player, leading to a 30% target share. Their OC David Blough comes from the Lions' tree and there was some Amon-Ra St. Brown stuff to Diggs' role. The Cowboys struggled with communication on these types of routes in Week 1.

Samuel's role was similar. There was a red-zone target on a Texas route from the backfield (first read), a quick out off play action (first read), second-and-1 out route (first read), a screen (first read) and a backfield choice route TD (broken play). That's good stuff!!! The Dolphins have the youngest defense by a mile, and rookie slot CB Chris Johnson was targeted 11 times in his debut, allowing two touchdowns. — Hayden Winks

Mayfield's rage leads to first top-5 week since 2024

After his big contract, people said the chip on Baker Mayfield 's shoulder disappeared in Week 1 versus Cincinnati . The best way to get that chip back is going against the team that drafted him in the Cleveland Browns . In 2022, Baker Mayfield was unstartable as the Panthers QB. However, he had one good game: 19 fantasy points versus the Browns, his season high.

I give out a lot of stats and this is most based on the stat that Baker Mayfield hates the Browns.

He now will face the QB who replaced him, and a defense that just allowed 11 yards per attempt to Trevor Lawrence . Mayfield is healthy, running again and set up for a bounce-back week against his former team. — Joel Smyth

So, here's the struggle of being a fan of a team. If Emeka Egbuka had torched my Bengals in Week 1, I'd be too bitter to write him up. But an 11.3-PPR-point outing and a Cincinnati W is the right combination for me to highlight how much of an issue the second-year receiver was beyond the box score. That offseason toe injury certainly wasn't a concern for Egbuka or OC Zac Robinson. On top of hoarding two-thirds of the team's air yards, the former Buckeye was everywhere along the formation, including a few snaps out of the backfield. Even in 11 personnel formations, it was Egbuka, not Chris Godwin Jr., with the highest target rate from the slot. And with half of his looks coming off play action, it's no wonder over half of his receptions turned into first downs.

But against the Browns, we should expect touchdowns instead. Not a single Cleveland CB forced an incompletion in Week 1. And its defensive front ranked fourth-worst in pressure rate. If this is going to be a "Baker Mayfield Revenge Game" like Joel suggests, above Mayfield's resurgence into the top five will only come with Egbuka finishing inside the top three. — Chris Allen

Skattebo handled 18 carries for 81 yards and a touchdown in Week 1, and what stood out was how different this Giants team looked with John Harbaugh at the helm. New York ran for 165 yards against Dallas and played with a physical identity that fits Skattebo perfectly. Now he gets a Rams defense that San Francisco just ran through, with Christian McCaffrey averaging 6.8 yards per carry, Kaelon Black averaging 4.6 and the 49ers piling up 174 rushing yards. That was with Myles Garrett on the field. Now Garrett is headed to IR following knee surgery. This Rams defense may be moving in a much different direction than we expected entering the season.

Give Skattebo another 18-plus touches in this environment and I think he turns them into a top-10 fantasy finish. — Ray Garvin

Garrett Wilson finishes as a top-five WR

We're back to business as usual with Garrett Wilson; he's the clear-cut target hog in the Jets offense. Wilson's 30.4% target share ranked eighth among all wide receivers and his 49% air yard share ranked ninth. The Jets went from 29th to seventh in rare of plays out of heavy personnel packages between the 2025 season and Week 1. We know that No. 1 receivers consolidate targets, especially downfield looks, in those groupings. With rookie first-round receiver Omar Cooper Jr. set to miss time and vacate the slot role, we can expect New York to work out of two tight end looks more often going forward with Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq. That will funnel more high-leverage looks to Wilson.

He'll see plenty of those this week against a Packers defense that has serious issues at cornerback and can't consistently rush the passer. The Jets' offensive line was excellent in Week 1 and should afford Geno Smith the time needed to launch it down the field to Garrett Wilson for a monster day in a contest that could be sneaky high-scoring. — Matt Harmon

For years we followed Kevin O'Connell everywhere, before the collapse of 2025. Perhaps last year's mess was all J.J. McCarthy 's fault. Kyler Murray 's debut was truncated after just 11 snaps, and if his concussion issues don't clear in time for Sunday, Wentz gets the juicy assignment against an injury-wrecked Chicago secondary. Wentz made good decisions in his relief appearance last week, reminding us of past days when O'Connell worked miracles with players like Nick Mullens and Joshua Dobbs . Wentz has a great shot at multiple touchdowns in this spot. — Scott Pianowski

Both 49ers RBs top 100 yards vs. Dolphins

Kyle Shanahan had an epiphany when it comes to Christian McCaffrey's early-season usage. Perhaps he witnessed the success the Seahawks had splitting RB touches last year, before eventually turning the backfield over to Kenneth Walker en route to a Super Bowl victory. Maybe it had to do with CMC missing time in August due to "general tightness" or the fact San Francisco had a big lead in the opener. Regardless, McCaffrey played 55% of the snaps and earned 15 touches, while his backup Kaelon Black was also given 15 touches on a 43% snap share. Neither player found the end zone in a tougher matchup with the Rams, but that won't be a problem this week against a Dolphins defense that just allowed 188 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns to the Raiders' tandem of Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr.

The 49ers are 13-point favorites in this contest, so there will be no need for McCaffrey to rack up unnecessary miles in the second half. That opens the door for CMC to start hot and Black to put this game away in the fourth quarter. While McCaffrey is always in your lineup when healthy, Black has quickly emerged as an upside RB3 with a much higher ceiling against soft opponents like Miami . — Justin Boone

Matthew Golden posts a second straight top 24 week

Matthew Golden closed drafts as the WR49 on Yahoo. So it makes sense that the market is slow to react to his 12 target, 6 reception, 95-yard Week 1 performance — which made him the WR20 on the week. As someone who ranked him closer to WR40 during the preseason, I feel that his consensus spot of WR33 ahead of Week 2 is an under-reaction.

The Packers pace was faster. Their neutral pass rate was higher. And, most notably, their run game was predictably suspect. All of those factors are directing us towards a pass first operation with a very clear top-two wide receivers, something that has been rare in the LaFleur era. Christian Watson 's WR11 consensus ranking is on point, but it still feels like you can get in on the ground floor with Golden's delayed rise. Congratulations, you drafted a WR2/3 at a WR5 price tag. — Josh Norris

articles.title: College Fantasy Football: Bold predictions for this weekend's Week 3 slate
articles.summary: Our college fantasy football analysts share their hot takes for Week 3.
articles.body:
Yahoo Sports College Football analysts Eric Froton and Nick Bromberg deliver their boldest college fantasy football predictions for the remaining Week 3 slate.

Ijeboi transferred out of Minnesota in the offseason with the intention of being a starting Big 10 running back. He has made the most of the opportunity, looking both strong and elusive in a 27-carry, 114 yard, 3-TD performance against Wake Forest last weekend.

This week, Purdue travels to face a UCLA defense that allowed a similarly proportioned Cal RB Adam Mohammed to run wild for 120 yards and a touchdown, along with seven receptions and 46 yards through the air. I think Ijeboi is able to run for 100+ yards and rack up 20 fantasy points in a very appealing B10 matchup against a beatable UCLA run D this weekend. — Froton

With a new coaching staff in town, led by longtime Penn State HC James Franklin, the Hokies throwing at top-25 rates on both standard and passing downs. The heavy pass script reflects the trust Franklin has in the cerebral QB Ethan Grunkemeyer , who started seven games in 2025 for Penn State in relief of Drew Allar , winning his last four. Reynolds leads all Power Four tight ends averaging 20.1 half-PPR points per game, and is also the Virginia Tech team leader in targets, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns — a rarity for a tight end in this day and age. With Reynolds being a star on the rise, I think Franklin feeds him with 8+ targets against a competitive Maryland team that can also score, which propels Reynolds to a 100+ yards, two-touchdown breakout performance versus Maryland. — Froton

Need another QB? Bet on Anthony Colandrea

The Cornhuskers QB had a breakout season in 2025 at UNLV and has gotten off to a hot start in 2026. He has thrown for seven touchdowns and just one interception through Nebraska 's first two games and has also added another rushing score. He's rostered in only 16% of Yahoo leagues.

Colandrea's performance is something Nebraska hasn't had at quarterback in a long, long time. He's become the first Cornhuskers quarterback to throw for three TDs in back-to-back games in a decade and there's no reason why he can't do it a third game in a row. Nebraska plays North Dakota in Week 3 before Big Ten play begins. — Bromberg

Believe it or not, the Terrapins have produced a fantasy-relevant receiving duo. Chris Durr Jr. and Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding are each among the top 10 in receptions through the first two weeks of the season. Durr has 16 grabs for 147 yards and a score, while Gladding has caught 14 passes for 187 yards and two touchdowns.

They should have success in Week 3, too. Virginia Tech allowed nine yards per pass attempt to Old Dominion in Week 2, and Malik Washington has already thrown 72 passes so far this season with a completion percentage of nearly 74%. — Bromberg

articles.body: The Asian Games 2026 will officially begin on Saturday, with the opening ceremony scheduled to start at 2:30pm IST in Nagoya. articles.title: Mike Sweetney, former Knicks player and Georgetown basketball star, dies at 43
articles.summary: Sweetney’s wife announced his death, remembering her husband of nearly 20 years and saying his children were “the light of
articles.body:
Sweetney's wife announced his death, remembering her husband of nearly 20 years and saying his children were "the light of his life."

Mike Sweetney, the former Georgetown standout who became the ninth overall pick in the 2003 NBA Draft, has died at 43. His wife, India, announcing his death on social media.

"With the heaviest hearts, we are deeply saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Michael," she wrote, adding that Sweetney had been her best friend for 30 years and her husband for almost 20. "His children were the light of his life," she said.

"No one loved him more and he loved no one more than his family. His children were the light of his life, and he lived every day to give them the best life possible. He's been my best friend for 30 years and my husband for almost 20. I'm not sure what we or I will do without him. He was the best son , brother, family member, friend, father and husband ANYONE could ask for," she continued.

A cause of death has not been publicly disclosed.

Sweetney built his reputation at Georgetown, where his physical presence and scoring ability made him one of the Big East's standout forwards in the early 2000s. Over three seasons, he averaged 18.2 points and 9.2 rebounds while shooting 54.4% from the field, according to Sports-Reference. He earned All-Big East honors twice and left Georgetown after his junior season to enter the NBA draft.

The New York Knicks selected Sweetney with the No. 9 pick in 2003. He spent his first two NBA seasons in New York before being traded to the Chicago Bulls in 2005.

Sweetney played four NBA seasons in total, appearing in 233 games with the Knicks and Bulls. He averaged 6.5 points and 4.5 rebounds over his professional career, according to the Associated Press.

His basketball career continued overseas after his NBA stint, before he eventually moved into coaching. Sweetney later joined Yeshiva University's men's basketball staff as an assistant coach, becoming a valued figure around the program and its players.

Yeshiva head coach Elliot Steinmetz remembered Sweetney as much more than a former NBA player, writing that "the world lost a giant today" and calling him a close friend and a member of the Yeshiva and Jewish communities.

Sweetney's death also prompted tributes from his former NBA teams and Georgetown, where he remains among the program's notable statistical performers. He finished his college career with 1,750 points and 887 rebounds.

From Georgetown's frontcourt to the NBA and later the coaching bench, Sweetney's basketball journey covered several chapters. His family's tribute now places the emphasis on a different legacy, a husband, father and friend whose impact extended well beyond the court.

articles.body:
ROME (AP) — Roberto Mancini called up 34 players on Friday to his first Italy squad since returning as coach , ahead of four Nations League games.

Mancini has been tasked with revitalising a team in crisis and his squad includes a mix of experienced players who he led to the European Championship title in 2021, and potential debutants.

Eight players are uncapped, Mohamed Ali Zoma, Antonio Vergara, Alessandro Romano, Issa Doumbia, Michael Kayode , Massimo Pessina, Samuele Inácio and Sebastiano Esposito .

The only squad limit in the league phase is that teams must submit a list of 23 before midnight ahead of each game, but they can change players between matches.

Italy starts at home to Belgium on Sept. 25 before playing Turkey three days later, France on Oct. 2 and Turkey again on Oct. 5.

Italy is in crisis after failing for a third straight time to qualify for the World Cup, prompting the resignations of FIGC president Gabriele Gravina and coach Gennaro Gattuso in April, shortly after the playoff defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Mancini was rehired as coach, three years after he abandoned the same job for a lucrative contract with Saudi Arabia .

articles.title: Marco Kasper Has One Year Left to Prove It
articles.summary: Marco Kasper enters the final year of his deal with the top-six job wide open. #RedWings
articles.body:
Detroit Red Wings center Marco Kasper is 22 years old and out of runway. Kasper went eighth overall in the 2022 NHL Draft, he enters 2026-27 on the last season of his entry-level contract, and he becomes a restricted free agent the moment the year ends.

He gets that year without Dylan Larkin in front of him, at least to start. Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff said Sept. 16 that Larkin, who requested a trade in June, suffered an upper-body injury in an off-ice session and would not skate when camp opened . Detroit has missed the playoffs 10 straight seasons , the longest active drought in the NHL. Somebody down the middle has to take the job.

Marco Kasper Has the Clearest Path to the Top Six

Tony Wolak of The Hockey Writers named Kasper one of four Red Wings with something to prove this season, alongside Lucas Raymond , Axel Sandin-Pellikka and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard. Wolak wrote:

Center Marco Kasper enters 2026-27 with perhaps the clearest opportunity of any Red Wings forward. After spending most of last season in a bottom-six role, he needs to prove that he belongs in the team's top six. That opportunity comes with responsibility. Kasper needs to show that he can handle tougher competition, contribute offensively and remain effective away from the puck. If he can do that and build on the 0.96 ixG/60 he produced last year, Kasper could establish himself as a long-term top-six center for Detroit.

Wolak tied the opening directly to Larkin's situation. If Detroit trades him, a hole opens near the top of the lineup, and Wolak argued Kasper is one of the players who could be asked to fill it .

Kasper finished last season with nine goals and 19 points in 81 games after posting 19 goals and 37 points in 77 games as a rookie, per ESPN . The Hockey News reported he played through injury for much of the year. The rest of the drop traces to deployment: bottom-six minutes limit both the quality and the volume of the chances a center sees.

The public projections do not have Kasper in the top six yet. Jake Tye of The Hockey News, working from Daily Faceoff and PuckPedia, put Kasper on the third line on Sept. 8 . Daily Faceoff lists him at center with Carter Mazur on his left wing; PuckPedia slides him to the wing with J.T. Compher in the middle. Both projections were built before Larkin got hurt. Camp is where Kasper changes them.

Kasper carries an $886,666 cap hit in the final year of the three-year entry-level deal he signed in July 2022. A 20-goal, 20-assist season settles the lineup argument and the contract negotiation in one stroke. Another year closer to 19 points, and Detroit is writing a bridge deal for a player it took eighth overall.

articles.title: Quinn Hughes isn’t sweating contract talks with the Wild, doesn’t see the season start as a deadline
articles.summary: Quinn Hughes unwound after an especially eventful hockey season with the usual retreat to his lake home in Michigan, soaking up the summer with his brothers...
articles.body:
ST. PAUL, Minn. — Quinn Hughes unwound after an especially eventful hockey season with the usual retreat to his lake home in Michigan, soaking up the summer with his brothers and their friends.

Hughes would prefer if everyone would relax about his contract situation, too.

As the star defenseman and Olympic gold medalist reported to his first training camp with the Minnesota Wild without an extension, raising the anxiety level at least within the fan base. Hughes said after the team's first practice that he's plenty satisfied with the direction and state of the organization and simply hasn't gotten around to thinking hard about the next phase of his career.

"With planning out my future, I don't do that. I don't really plan out my summer," Hughes said. "Just kind of went about it and enjoyed it."

Hughes is in the final year of his current deal with a $7.85 million salary cap hit. His agent, Pat Brisson, and Wild general manager Bill Guerin have begun talks about a new contract, but for Hughes the start of the regular season on Oct. 1 is just a superficial deadline.

"I don't feel stressed to do something before the season," Hughes said. "And that's not saying that something won't happen, but that's just how it is."

Fellow defenseman Cale Makar of the Colorado Avalanche set the bar for annual average value at $20.5 million by signing the richest deal in league history, but Hughes might well top that, particularly on a shorter-term contract.

Hughes has fueled some speculation about desiring to play with younger brothers Jack and Luke, who are both with New Jersey , but he's only 26 and should have ample time left to link up with them down the road.

"I'm really happy here. I love the guys. I love the team, and I fit in really well," Hughes said. "Obviously, there's a draw to play with those guys at some point, but I think Jack said it perfectly: I'm not going to sacrifice a great spot for me to play with them."

Left wing Marcus Foligno , whose older brother Nick was acquired by the Wild right before the trade deadline last season, has been reminding Hughes that he can wait to figure out where to play with Jack and Luke. Marcus is 35 and Nick will turn 39 in October.

"It's the best when it's toward the end of the career," Foligno said. "You do it too early, you don't appreciate it as much. It's great when you're just hanging on."

After arriving in Minnesota near midseason in a trade with Vancouver , Hughes helped lead the U.S. national team to the gold medal at the Olympics in Italy about two months later. Then in just 48 games with the Wild, he set the franchise defenseman record with 53 points and was an integral part of their first-round victory over Dallas that was the first playoff series win in 11 years.

Guerin was general manager of the U.S. team, too, so he's developed a strong relationship with Hughes, who offered no hint of dissatisfaction, impatience or uncertainty on the subject of wanting to re-up with the Wild.

"I have so much trust in Billy. He's a great GM. He's always going to address the needs of the team. It's not like I have to freaking poke at Billy to do something," Hughes said. "Billy's kind of a shark. He's going to be trying to make our team better at every point he can."

articles.title: FSU exploring the possibility of Jimbo Fisher returning as head coach
articles.summary: With the struggles that Florida State has had under head coach Mike Norvell, they're looking into a return for Jimbo Fisher to the program.
articles.body:
Times around the Florida State football program are hard. Head coach Mike Norvell simply isn't getting it done as the team has gone 8-18 since 2023, with a 3-14 record in the ACC and a current nine-game road losing streak.

The standard at FSU is extremely high, and in order to return to dominance, it's clear that they need to go in another direction. With that said, according to Bruce Feldman of The Athletic , Florida State is exploring a possible return for Jimbo Fisher as head coach.

One interesting development we've heard recently is the prospect of former Florida State coach Jimbo Fisher returning to take over the program. The 60-year-old Fisher, who led the Seminoles to the national title to cap the 2013 season and then oversaw the beginning of the program's backslide a few years later before taking the Texas A&M job, really wants the job, we've heard.

Industry sources told The Athletic that FSU brass is looking into the possibility. Financially, it could make some sense. As we reported earlier this year, FSU wasn't aggressive at all in the portal this offseason with a nod toward saving its money for something else down the road. That something else could be paying some of the near $50 million the school would owe Norvell if he were fired. Then there's the money FSU would need to hire a new staff and perhaps to buy out a new coach. (Duke's Manny Diaz, a Florida State grad, could be an option, too.)

Fisher was very successful at Florida State with an 83-23 record in eight seasons. That included three ACC titles (2012-2014), a 29-game win streak, and, of course, the program's third national championship in 2013 when they went 14-0. Also, FSU made the first-ever College Football Playoff in 2014.

Although he's been away from coaching since 2023, Fisher is very aware of where the landscape of college football is today and what it takes to be successful. Plus, and more importantly, he knows what it takes in Tallahassee.

One area that FSU needs to improve in is recruiting, and they haven't had a top-10 recruiting class in quite some time. Fisher was an excellent recruiter and knew how to build relationships, and that's essential when it comes to that aspect.

This topic will certainly heat up if Florida State loses to the Alabama Crimson Tide this weekend.

articles.summary: "I'm still scratching my head about why he isn't in that squad regularly at the moment," said BBC Radio Nottingham's Colin Fray after finding out that Morgan...
articles.body:
"I'm still scratching my head about why he isn't in that squad regularly at the moment," said BBC Radio Nottingham's Colin Fray after finding out that Morgan Gibbs-White had once again missed out on a place in the England squad.

Thomas Tuchel said the Nottingham Forest player was not included in his squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures because "it does not make sense" to pick any more number 10s.

But Gibbs-White, who scored 15 goals and registered four assists last season, has accumulated more goal involvements than any other English midfielder this calendar year.

He has also already netted one goal and contributed two assists in Nottingham Forest's opening four games of the 2026-27 campaign.

On how close the 26-year-old was to being selected, Tuchel said: "It was close, but it is always the case. It makes no sense to nominate four or five number 10s. It just doesn't help anyone.

"We can see the form he is in. He ended last season very strongly, he was a key player in Nottingham Forest avoiding relegation, and we can see him stepping up now.

"It is one thing to be nominated, like Cole Palmer getting his ticket back into the squad, but it is another thing to perform for England - and that also counts."

Speaking on the Shut Up And Show More Football podcast, Fray said: "He can't do much more to get into the England squad, but was I entirely surprised by the decision? No, not really.

"Tuchel knew the form he was in at the end of last season and he still didn't take him to the World Cup.

"His numbers for 2026 are unparalleled by an English player. I also believe, as a midfielder, he is leading the way in terms of goals and assists this calendar year across Europe's top five leagues.

"He is doing everything he can, so I think it says a lot about their relationship.

"Tuchel said he didn't want to pick four or five number 10s, which I get, but who are the ones in the best form? Gibbs-White is indisputably at the top of every list right now, so you just cannot make that argument, in my opinion."

articles.title: Why Lamar Jackson might have some trouble in Ravens vs. Saints matchup
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson's Week 2 matchup isn't as clean as it might seem on the surface.
articles.body:
After a blowout Week 1 win, the Baltimore Ravens enter Week 2 with a 1-0 record and a matchup against the New Orleans Saints .

While the Ravens are favored to win this game, and should be, there are some issues for Baltimore in this matchup. Zay Flowers is banged up and might not play, and even if he does, he's not likely to be 100%. Ja'Kobi Lane is out and already on IR.

However, the WR room isn't the only thing for Jackson and the Ravens to worry about. As ESPN research highlighted, the Saints' defensive scheme matches up well against Jackson and could give him some trouble in this upcoming matchup.

Lamar Jackson could face issues from Saints defense

"The Saints played zone defense on 38 of 40 dropbacks (95%) in Week 1, per NFL Next Gen Stats," ESPN shared. "Since the start of last season, quarterback Lamar Jackson is third in QBR versus man coverage (83.6) and 23rd in QBR versus zone coverage (44.2) among 28 qualified QBs."

This statistic from ESPN is a noteworthy one, as the Saints defense, which played mostly zone against the Detroit Lions in Week 1, is likely to play mostly zone in Week 2 against the Ravens.

Jackson is not as good against zone coverage as he is against man, and with the Saints rarely utilizing man coverage, this could be a bit of a tricky matchup for Jackson.

He and the Ravens still have the tools to win this matchup; it just might not be as smooth sailing and dominant as their Week 1 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts .

Ravens fans should not panic about Jackson, as he'll still likely play great. But it shouldn't be a surprise if Jackson does struggle a little bit more than usual, especially with a banged-up WR corps.

With his production nearly halved when facing zone versus man coverage, his play on Sunday will be something worth keeping a close eye on. If he thrives, then this might be the year for the Ravens.

articles.summary: Florida forward Brad Marchand is expected to miss the first month of the season, meaning the 38-year-old will be sidelined for the Panthers’ first 14 games,...
articles.body:
FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. — Florida forward Brad Marchand is expected to miss the first month of the season, meaning the 38-year-old will be sidelined for the Panthers' first 14 games, at minimum, while continuing to recover from offseason surgery.

Marchand revealed in mid-August that he had surgery, the details of which have not been released. He was dogged by a lower-body issue for much of last season when Florida's hopes of contending for what would have been a third consecutive Stanley Cup were derailed by injuries throughout the lineup.

"He's going to take the month of October for rehab," Panthers coach Paul Maurice said after the team's first day of training camp. "That may mean he's ready to play right at the end of it. That may mean he needs a short period of time, assuming no setbacks. But we're planning on rehabbing for October."

Marchand missed a career-high 30 games last season. He was effective — with 27 goals and 27 assists for 54 points in 52 games — before getting shut down in early March, around the time it became clear that Florida was not going to qualify for the playoffs.

Marchand was on the ice, though not in either of the two sessions that Florida used for its first day of camp. He went through a separate workout with forward Jonah Gadjovich , who was limited to 10 games last season before having neck surgery.

Gadjovich remains out indefinitely, Maurice said.

"There's a couple of things that we're trying to get sorted out," Maurice said. "Clearly, it's been a long-term issue for us and it hasn't resolved, so we're still looking at different options and searching for some answers on this to see if we can get him back playing. He's skating, as you saw, so we're not concerned with that. But we'll list him as out indefinitely."

articles.title: LeSean McCoy says Pat McAfee is second-most powerful person in America
articles.summary: Only Donald Trump has more power than Pat McAfee right now.
articles.body:
Pat McAfee was seen on ESPN earlier this week. While that's not an unusual occurrence, seeing someone smoking something is unusual in 2026. McAfee was shown setting something down on his desk that was still smoking. It doesn't really matter what exactly it was , it sticks out like a sore thumb. And it's yet another example of there being different rules for McAfee at ESPN.

One person who is no longer surprised is LeSean McCoy who proclaimed McAfee the second most powerful person in America behind Donald Trump after seeing this. It may sound like an exaggeration, but he makes a pretty effective case while also making sure to point out how outrageous it is that this is a kicker we're talking about here.

"Pat is a kicker, bro. Pat gets done kickin' and he's more popular than any quarterback that's retired other than Tom Brady , for one," said McCoy on his podcast. "For two is, he is probably the most powerful person other than Donald Trump. He the only dude that I know that can smoke weed on his show and nothing happens. Call out his boss and then get a raise. He can do whatever he want. So listen, I'm a fan of Pat. I've always been a fan of Pat, bro. The stuff he's doing right now, nobody's done. He's great on TV. Great personality. Imagine a kicker doing these type of things. I root for Pat. Like I said before, ain't nobody more powerful than him, other than the president."

How can you not listen to this and go through the Alonzo Mourning gif of emotions as you realize he might actually be right? Obviously, there's a big gulf between running the country and running ESPN, but when they needed to get that Protect College Sports Act voted on, who did they turn to? When Donald Trump needed to get some publicity for that made-up athletic competition , who did he turn to? The guy with the country rap album who is prominently featured on the pregame shows for the two biggest sports in America, college football and professional football.

There might be people in this country with more power than Pat McAfee, but if you watch ESPN, you probably wouldn't be able to tell.

articles.title: Highs and Lows: Mariners at Rockies Series Preview
articles.summary: The Mariners head to Colorado to face the Rockies this weekend.
articles.body:
The Mariners have entered that phase of the season where they're just playing out the remaining games without much purpose beyond fulfilling the MLB schedule. The last time the M's were playing irrelevant games this early in September was during the pandemic-shortened season in 2020. It's been so long, I almost forgot what it was like to be in this limbo state.

The Rockies are well acquainted with playing irrelevant games, however. The last time they were truly competitive was back in 2018 when they won 91 games. Since then, the team has been in the midst of a long and arduous rebuilding cycle that doesn't seem like it's anywhere close to ending. After reaching a nadir seven years into this cycle with 119 losses last year, the team finally made a change atop the organization, hiring Paul DePodesta to lead the baseball operations department. The team is on track to make a 16 win improvement over last year — a small but meaningful step forward — but the work of building another contender in Colorado will continue for the foreseeable future.

Here's a crazy stat: the Rockies' .325 wOBA as a team is the highest it's been since 2019. Over the past six years, despite playing in a stadium that boosts offense to ridiculous levels, the team has put up a .308 wOBA, 21st in baseball during that period. Last year's breakout from Hunter Goodman and this year's breakout from TJ Rumfield have gone a long way toward improving the lineup. Those two batters are dramatically different in approach; Goodman is a traditional power hitter with huge home run totals to go along with a huge strikeout rate. Rumfield is more measured in his approach, content to take a walk and put the ball in play to take advantage of the huge outfield in Coors Field. Cole Carrigg and Kyle Karros are another pair of youngsters who have shown a lot of promise this year. There are glimpses of a competent lineup here.

The Rockies don't have a starter listed for Friday's game at the time of publication but I expect Ryan Feltner to take some portion of the bulk innings. He had been a member of the Rockies' rotation for most of the year but has been shifted to the bullpen in a long relief role recently. He pitched on Tuesday in relief of Kyle Freeland and spun five shutout innings against the Padres. At one point back in 2024, he looked like he had figured out how to find some success pitching at altitude — he posted a 4.49 ERA and a 4.16 FIP in 30 starts that season — but a series of injuries last year derailed that progress. He's been mostly healthy this season, but his effectiveness has waned and now the team is reevaluating where he fits on the roster.

It must be totally demoralizing to be a pitching prospect in the Rockies organization. You put in all the work to make your way through the minors up to the big leagues and then face the toughest pitching environment in baseball. Gabriel Hughes made his debut in July and has actually pitched pretty well all things considered — his park-adjusted FIP is better than league average at 92. Unfortunately, his ERA is more than two runs higher at 6.37. His fastball has a really interesting movement profile; it doesn't fade arm-side like most four-seams tend to do. Instead, it has a bit of cut to it so that it's almost arrow-straight from a three-quarters arm slot. Opposing batters find it extremely hard to square up even if they have no problem making contact with it.

Every rebuilding team needs a veteran innings eater or two to soak up as many innings as possible during the season. That's Tomoyuki Sugano's job this year. After coming over from NBP last year, he's posted nearly identical 5.36 and 5.49 FIPs over the last two seasons while making 57 starts for the Orioles and Rockies. He's got a deep repertoire that features a solid splitter, three variations on a breaking ball, and three very hittable fastballs. It's a problem when all three of your fastballs feature expected wOBAs that start with a four.

On Wednesday, the Astros and Rangers were tied atop the AL West standings, but separated by a game after Houston won and Texas lost on Thursday. The Astros host the Braves and the Rangers host the Blue Jays this weekend.

articles.title: Cowboys want a better defense, but the Commanders might have got one
articles.summary: How confident have you seen Commanders fans this week?
articles.body:
Time for a bounce-back game from the Dallas Cowboys . If that is to happen, it will come at the expense of the Washington Commanders . To see if that might happen, we checked in with Andrew Y. over at Hogs Haven for the lowdown on the Commanders heading into the second week of the season.

Blogging The Boys: What were some of the best things that you saw from the Commanders in the first game versus Philadelphia that bode well for the season?

Hogs Haven: I think the first thing almost any Commanders fan would say is the performance of the defense. Last year, the Commanders had one of the worst defenses in the NFL, so they completely overhauled it in the offseason, with a new DC in Daronte Jones (who brings an attacking Flores-like scheme) and replacing over half of the starters on defense. Early returns indicate the overhaul has paid off. The defense was living in the Eagles backfield last Sunday, generating a 48.48% pressure rate on Jalen Hurts and a 24% TFL rate, both notably higher than NFL average. On offense, things were a bit of a mixed bag, but there were a few positives. Other fans may disagree, but I saw a lot of positives in the way Jayden Daniels played. He played like more of a pocket QB, avoiding pressure by navigating the pocket and avoiding pressure like a ninja while keeping his eyes downfield. He didn't make a lot of connections passing until the 4th quarter, but I blame that more on the playcalling and the quality of the Eagles defense. Playing from the pocket instead of breaking the pocket when nothing is immediately available should do a better job of keeping Jayden healthy. It was also notable that the OL played competently. A lot of people were worried that with the injury to Laremy Tunsil and former backup IOL Nick Allegretti starting at Center that the OL would be one of the worst in the league and would prevent the offense from functioning. I don't think that was the case. The OL seemed competent, perhaps more at the league average level. That was a win compared to expectations.

articles.title: NY Giants-Rams matchup: Los Angeles offense will provide stern test
articles.summary: The New York Giants travel to Los Angeles to play the Rams — can they carry their momentum from Week 1?sports
articles.body:
The New York Giants travel to Los Angeles for their second consecutive prime-time game, where they will face the 0-1 Rams . Los Angeles is coming off a disappointing 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia on Thursday night. The Rams' decision to travel to Australia just 28 hours before kickoff drew heavy scrutiny after San Francisco dominated the game, holding a seven-minute advantage in time of possession and out-gaining Los Angeles by 89 yards.

Nevertheless, Los Angeles remains a top team in the NFL, and they've had over a week to stew on the loss, but they did lose star defensive end Myles Garrett to a knee injury. Injuries are a factor, of course, but one of the crucial factors in the game will be the trenches, and the Rams offensive line struggled against the 49ers.

The Rams blew assignments on the offensive line, and Raheem Morris' defense was harrassing, although they failed to sack future Hall of Famer Matt Stafford .

The Giants have the personnel to be a top-five pass rush in the league, especially if Abdul Carter lives up to his insanely high potential. Dallas focused on Brian Burns in Week 1 — will Sean McVay's offense do the same?

The Rams have a physical and big offensive line that can command the point of attack. Alaric Jackson (LT) and Steve Avila (LG) are a quality tandem on the left side, with Warren McClendon Jr. (RT) and Kevin Dotson (RG) on the right. Coleman Shelton centers the line. One of the biggest matchups in the game, quite possibly, is D.J. Reader against the interior offensive line.

Reader was outstanding in Week 1 for the Giants, and he'll have to be again against a team that will try to run DUO and displace, while marrying its run game to its dynamic passing attack. Overall, the Giants must be on their P's and Q's up front. The Rams' receivers block their back side off, and I expect to see a heavy dose of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum .

The Giants' pass rush can certainly take advantage of the pair of tackles, and the speed of Carter and Burns could look to win against the more power-based line that the Rams possess, but the strength of players like Dotson and Avila could easily give the edge to Los Angeles.

Los Angeles will frequently use 12/13 personnel with a combination of the four tight ends: Colby Parkenson, Tyler Higbee , Terrance Ferguson , and Davis Allen ( if healthy, was concussed in Week 1 ). The Rams were in 13 personnel on 44% of their snaps in Week 1. They took a big deficit and played 11 personnel at a 46% rate, but expect heavier usage in neutral game scripts, which will prompt the Giants to use their five-man front with Tremaine Edmunds and Arvell Reese on the backside.

A combination of these players would join Reader up front with the first-team base package: Chauncey Golston , Shelby Harris , Kayvon Thibodeaux , Abdul Carter, and Brian Burns. The Giants did spell Harris and Reader with Darius Alexander and C.J. Okoye — I will be very nervous when that happens against the Rams. Alexander and Okoye were liabilities up front, and McVay will attack them with DUO.

Kyren Williams saw 13 carries to Blake Corum's 10; the former averaged 3.7 yards on the ground with 2.09 yards after contact and a touchdown, while the latter averaged 5.4 yards on the ground with 1.50 yards after contact. This dynamic duo will be a threat in DUO.

The rushing attack will set up play-action shots to the Rams' receivers. McVay will use 11 personnel to get Dru Phillips on the field, where he'll likely see Davante Adams in the slot — this is a mismatch to exploit. Stretch-zone play-action passes outside the numbers to displace and get the Giants moving away from the throw will be a successful option for McVay if the Giants start to buckle against the run.

Then there's Puka Nacau. He aligned at just a 12.5% rate in the slot, but I can see him moving there for his blocking and the mismatch against Phillips. He only caught five of his nine targets for 74 yards in Week 1. The Giants' cornerbacks will be tested against Nacua, Adams, and Stafford.

Similar to Dak Prescott , I don't think we'll see many blitzes, but there will be simulated pressures and twists in defensive passing-favorable situations. Stafford is quick to see the field and still has a cannon attached to him, so the field is his oyster. The third receiver in 11 personnel will likely be a combination of Jordan Whittington , Konata Mumpfield , or Xavier Smith .

Tight end Terrance Ferguson, though, is a player to circle and watch when, and if, the Rams start to run the football in their heavy personnel. Ferguson is an athletic tight end who is a threat off play action.

Dennard Wilson will likely mix Cover-4 and Cover-3, but may need to rely more on Cover-3 to get the safety closer in the box, depending on how successful the Rams are running the football. Wilson will likely through some curveballs at Stafford, and either Burns or Carter will align across the formation to try and gain a speed advantage, but it all comes down to stopping the run against these Rams — which, of course — is an issue when they have the receiving weapons and quarterback that they possess.

The Giants are 7.5-point road underdogs with an Over/Under of 48ish ( depending on the book ). I feel a lot better about this matchup for the Giants after Week 1, but the Rams are a true test. If the Giants pull off this upset, they will vault themselves into the true contender conversation in the NFC. These are bright lights, but this is a different Giants' team coached by John Harbaugh and led by second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart .

While Evgeni Malkin was holding what could be his final annual training camp interview session with local reporters Friday at the UPMC Lemieux Sports Complex, PHN took the opportunity to speak one-on-one with another of the team's longtime core players.

Defenseman Kris Letang , the Penguins' other alternate captain along with Malkin , and team captain Sidney Crosby have at least the 2026-27 season to play together again, their North American pro sports record 21 st season as a trio with the same team.

Letang, while appreciating another season together, isn't feeling nostalgic or emotional about it. He isn't pondering whether this will be the end of their ride together after so many seasons and three Stanley Cups.

"We don't read that stuff. We don't worry about that stuff," Letang said. "If they want to talk about it every year, they can, but to us we try to live in the moment. We don't look too far ahead."

Letang and Crosby are 39, Malkin 40. After the Penguins lost to the Philadelphia Flyers in the first round of the playoffs last spring, only Letang and Crosby were under contract for this season. Malkin later signed a one-year extension for $5.5 million.

"Obviously, last season he had a great season. He deserved to get another shot and another contract based on his performance," Letang said. "I'm glad that he's doing it with us."

Before it was settled that Malkin would be playing for the Penguins again, he created some shock waves when he said that if things didn't work out with his original team, he would consider playing this season with another NHL team.

"I mean, if he still has the desire to play hockey and the Penguins were not going to sign him, I don't see why (he would) not (consider playing elsewhere) if you want to keep playing hockey," Letang said.

"It would be weird to see him in a different uniform, but sometimes if it's your fate, there's nothing you can do. If the team goes in a different direction, you're not in charge of those decisions so you can turn around and do what you have to do.

"It worked out, but he put (up) a pretty good season and I didn't see why the Penguins would not want him back."

Letang, who had three goals, 34 points in 74 games last season, is signed for this and one more season. He said he has not altered his approach to training camp after all these years.

"It's always pretty intense," he said. "Guys are excited. Guys are pretty anxious also. It's pretty fun. I just kind of prepare the same way I always did. I try to train hard so I get ready every season."

Famous for his intense offseason training, Letang does try a few new things from time to time.

He thrilled some local players when he showed up a couple times to skate in a 3V3 Elite League at local rink Ice Castle.

"It was cool," Letang said. "I kind of use it as a conditioning (opportunity). It's three-on-three, full ice, so it's a lot of skating."

He also was featured in a video doing backward, uphill lunges while holding a 90-pound weight in each hand. He shrugged when asked about that.

"you look like you have a six-pack on your quads" 👀 (🎥: IG/benbrunotraining & IG/jonchaimberg) #NHL #hockey #sports #workout #KrisLetang

"You try different things sometimes with different trainers," he said.

Now it's back to the real thing, two days into a shortened, intense training camp.

Letang has been paired with newcomer Trevor van Riemsdyk , who, like Letang, is a right-handed shot. The Penguins have an imbalance of righties and lefties, so van Riemsdyk is skating on his off side, something he said he is comfortable with.

There have been a couple times earlier in his career that Letang was asked to switch over to the left side, with less than stellar results. He also has been paired occasionally with a right-handed shot defense partner playing on his off side (We remember ye, Ben Lovejoy ).

"He doesn't ask who's going to play left. He just goes there," Letang said. "You feel like it's already natural for him."

articles.summary: Carlos Baleba return offers Manchester United a needed boostManchester United may finally be about to see Carlos Baleba in action, and that matters. When a c...
articles.body:
Carlos Baleba return offers Manchester United a needed boost

Manchester United may finally be about to see Carlos Baleba in action, and that matters. When a club spends £70 million on a midfielder, the expectation is immediate impact. So far, injury has got in the way.

The 22-year-old arrived from Brighton in the summer, carrying both a sizeable fee and a clear brief, add energy, power and control to a midfield that has lacked all three at key moments. An ankle problem picked up in pre-season has delayed that plan, but the situation has shifted quickly.

Earlier in the week, Michael Carrick suggested Baleba was nearing a return to full training, with post-international break minutes seen as the realistic target. Now the United manager has gone further. Baleba is in contention for this weekend, which changes the conversation around a team that badly needs a lift.

United's start has been poor. Four points from four Premier League matches is not where they expected to be, and a home defeat to Brighton in the Carabao Cup has added more noise around Carrick's position. That is what happens at a club of this size. Results dictate the mood.

Baleba's possible return does not solve everything, but it gives United a different profile in midfield, athletic, aggressive and capable of driving the game forward. At a time when the side has looked short of rhythm, that is useful.

There is also some encouragement on Luke Shaw. The left-back has missed the last three matches after last featuring in the 2-2 draw at Everton . Carrick said of Shaw: "It is really short term [with Shaw] but it is just working towards the game."

That is cautious rather than definitive, but it suggests Shaw is close. United need bodies back, and they need quality back even more.

Carrick knows the scrutiny is there, but his message has been straightforward. "We've got to put things in perspective: it's not a catastrophe or a disaster, it's not the end of the world, we've lost a couple of games recently.

"We feel we've started and been in all the games we've played, if not being the better team at the start of games. We're not having a real struggle all the time.

"We've done a lot of good things, the belief comes from that. The good things we've done get lose in the surrounding feeling but they don't get lost by us."

Fair enough. The problem for Manchester United is simple, sentiment does not buy time, results do. If Carlos Baleba is fit enough to contribute now, United need him involved.

articles.title: Star Boston Celtics forward Jayson Tatum shed more light on Achilles return
articles.summary: Tatum talked about what it was like to come back from such a severe injury and the support he had from peers along the way.
articles.body:
Star Boston Celtics forward Jayson Tatum shed some more light on how he bounced back from his Achilles tendon injury sustained in the 2025 NBA Eastern Conference Playoffs vs. the New York Knicks , focusing on his eventual return to the court and how he got to that moment.

Speaking in a recent interview with the eponymous host of the "Dan Patrick Show," Tatum talked about what it was like to come back from such a severe injury and the support he had from peers along the way. "I obviously talked to ( Kevin Durant ), Damian Lillard , and Tyrese Halliburton," said the St. Louis native.

"We were all … Dame (Lillard) was (injured with an Achilles tendon tear) a few weeks before me. Tyrese Halliburton was a few weeks after me. I talked to Dame a lot just because he was three, four weeks ahead of me, so I was curious about how his transition was, what his next steps were. All of us being in the same boat around the same time, (we were) being helpful to each other."

Tatum shared that even with such stellar (and informed on a personal level) support, he was apprehensive returning to the court. "I was nervous …," he recalled.

"I was anxious. To be honest, I was nervous every game that I played in this past season. I think I played in 20 or 21, including the playoffs … it had been a long time. But I was glad I went out there. I proved to myself, even if I was at 80 percent … that I could be effective. And I knew that given a long offseason, that I would be back to myself this October."

The Duke alum also spoke about overcoming the psychological aspect of returning from such a devastating injury.

"Physically, in this day and age, especially in professional sports with the best trainers and doctors and modern medicine, physically you're going to recover and you're going to be clear at the plate," explained Tatum.

"It's all it's the mental hurdle that is the toughest, and that is different for everyone and it just takes time. And only you can understand and know when you're 100 percent ready, when you're confident; nobody else can do that for you."

articles.title: 3 offensive keys for Texas A&M against Kentucky in Week 3
articles.summary: Texas A&M must establish the run, improve on third down and protect Marcel Reed to find consistency against Kentucky.
articles.body:
Texas A&M will open SEC play Saturday when it hosts Kentucky at Kyle Field. The Aggies are 2-0, but their offense still has plenty to clean up after producing only 255 total yards against Arizona State.

The passing game has looked promising when Marcel Reed has time to throw, but the offensive line and running backs have yet to find a consistent rhythm. Kentucky's defense has recorded six sacks and held opponents to 3.1 yards per carry, so Texas A&M cannot expect everything to correct itself.

Here are three offensive keys for the Aggies against the Wildcats.

Texas A&M rushed for only 92 yards on 35 carries against Arizona State, averaging 2.6 yards per attempt. Some of those struggles can be attributed to four new starters along the offensive line still learning to play together, but the Aggies need to determine which concepts fit their personnel before the schedule gets more difficult.

Kentucky has allowed only 107 rushing yards per game, so establishing the run will not come easily . Texas A&M does not have to dominate on the ground, but consistent production would keep the offense ahead of the chains and create more opportunities for Reed through play action.

The Aggies converted only 3-of-12 third downs against Arizona State and are 10-of-26 through two games. Those missed opportunities prevented the offense from sustaining drives and contributed to A&M entering the fourth quarter with only a four-point lead.

Kentucky has allowed its opponents to convert 13-of-26 third downs, giving offensive coordinator Holmon Wiggins an opportunity to exploit one of the Wildcats' early weaknesses. Better production on first and second down would also create manageable situations and allow Wiggins to use more of his playbook .

Key 3: Protect Marcel Reed and start faster

Kentucky has recorded six sacks through two games, and former Texas A&M defensive coordinator Jay Bateman will likely look for ways to pressure and confuse Reed. The Aggies' passing game has shown it can create explosive plays when Reed has time, making protection one of the most important factors in the matchup.

Texas A&M has taken too long to find its offensive rhythm in each of its first two games and cannot continue relying on its defense to provide touchdowns and short fields. An early scoring drive would settle the offense, force Kentucky to play from behind and give the Aggies' defense more opportunities to attack.
