articles.title: Why Pittsburgh's knack for big plays hides real issues
articles.summary: While T.J. Watt keeps rescuing the Pittsburgh Steelers, relying on late-game splash plays is not a sustainable long-term strategy.
articles.body:
Winning in the NFL is never easy, but the Pittsburgh Steelers have perfected a style of victory that feels equal parts thrilling and precarious. Time and again, Pittsburgh's teams have managed to pull out victories in games where they are statistically outplayed, relying on timely, game-flipping splash plays from their defensive stars to bail them out of structural flaws.

As the Steelers prepare for their Week 2 clash against the New England Patriots , national analysts are once again pointing out this familiar pattern. Reflecting on Pittsburgh's recent performances, " Pro Football Talk " co-host Michael Holley noted that Pittsburgh's record often paints a far prettier picture than its down-to-down execution warrants.

"The Steelers should have lost to the Falcons," Holley said. " Cooper Rush at quarterback, they should have lost to the Falcons. Now, the Steelers have displayed yet again that knack for making the big plays in the big spots, which is why they beat the Patriots last year. Even though the Patriots outplayed them, they have that uncanny sense of when to make the big play."

That "uncanny sense" is driven by elite individual talents like T.J. Watt and Cameron Heyward , who possess the rare ability to destroy an opponent's drive with a single strip-sack or key third-down stop.

But relying on late-game heroics isn't a sustainable strategy over a 17-game season. When an offense stalls or struggles to sustain drives, the defense is eventually forced to play too many snaps, shrinking the margin for error to zero.

While clutch playmaking is a hallmark of Pittsburgh football, leaning on it too heavily masks deeper operational vulnerabilities. If the Steelers want to transition from scrappy regular-season survivors to legitimate postseason contenders, they must start winning games on execution rather than waiting for another miracle play to save them.

articles.title: Bo Nix says Broncos won’t panic or freak out after season-opening loss
articles.summary: "We’re not starting from scratch or anything," Broncos QB Bo Nix said after the team's season-opening loss.
articles.body:
The 0-1 Denver Broncos still believe they are who they think they are after a Week 1 blowout loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Quarterback Bo Nix shared his thoughts about the place and mindset the team is in heading into a tough Week 2 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars (1-0).

"I learned a long time ago, you never play as bad as you think and you never play as good as you think," Nix said on Thursday after practice. "For us, it was the case of we didn't play as bad as what we thought. We just there at the end of the game, we didn't make third-down conversions. We felt like it was 7-7, 14-7 and 21-7 for a long time in the game. So it was reachable, and we were in it for a while. We just didn't help ourselves by any means. You watch the film, and there are a couple good things and then all of a sudden we're back because of a penalty or something. You just can't win this league like that."

Nix and Co. know there is a significant number of issues the Broncos will have to clean up in order to win in Week 2 and beyond. However, the challenge in front of them is not too daunting to be overcome.

"We're not going to press the panic button and we're not freaking out," Nix said. "We're not starting from scratch or anything. We're still in a good spot, and we just didn't play great by any means and we've got to play better."

The Broncos have the opportunity to show if the progress they've made over the week is enough to beat the 1-0 Jaguars, a team that beat Denver by 14 on their home turf in 2025.

articles.title: Is Joey Porter Jr. using Jalen Ramsey's trade exit playbook?
articles.summary: Joey Porter Jr.'s lingering back issue and contract stalemate with the Pittsburgh Steelers draw striking parallels to Jalen Ramsey's trade strategy.
articles.body:
When Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. walked off the practice field clutching his back, the collective reaction around the NFL went beyond simple concern for his health. Inside the building and across the league, observers began recognizing a familiar, high-stakes negotiation strategy, one that mirrors a famous trade-forcing blueprint.

For those tracking the standoff, Porter's tactics bear an uncanny resemblance to the way star cornerback Jalen Ramsey orchestrated his departure from the Jacksonville Jaguars. Ramsey famously leveraged a lingering back injury to sit out until Jacksonville granted his trade request.

On the " Kaboly and Mack " podcast, media insider Mark Kaboly and his co-host Chris Mack dissected the uncanny similarities and questioned who might be directing Porter's ongoing hold-in strategy.

While Porter's mild-mannered personality makes this aggressive posture surprising, the outside influences surrounding him offer significant context.

"My question is, I mean, knowing Joey, talking to him, he does not seem like this guy. This seems like a, you know, somebody in a fake body in here just doing this, which leads me to believe. it could be multiple people," Kaboly observed. "Who's in his ear? Obviously the agent, obviously his dad's advising him in some way."

Kaboly also highlighted a direct connection to Ramsey, the former All-Pro cornerback that another local media member recently mentioned.

"Joe Starkey mentioned this the other day. Jalen Ramsey forced his way out of Jacksonville in a very similar way. And Jalen Ramsey and JPJ are tight. I don't want to accuse anything of this happening. But once again, the optics look bad of a back injury forcing you out of Jacksonville to another team where you get paid," said Kaboly.

Whether guided by family advice, agency representation, or peer mentorship from Ramsey, Porter appears to be following a playbook designed to force the front office's hand. However, attempting to execute such a high-risk hold-in in Pittsburgh carries immense narrative risks for a young star.

articles.title: Czechs level Davis Cup tie against USA as South Korea eye Finals
articles.summary: Jiri Lehecka brought the Czech Republic level in their Davis Cup qualifier against the United States on Friday, after South Korea moved to the brink of a fir...
articles.body:
Jiri Lehecka brought the Czech Republic level in their Davis Cup qualifier against the United States on Friday, after South Korea moved to the brink of a first quarter-finals appearance.

Lehecka beat US Open runner-up Ben Shelton 6-4, 6-4 in Prague as the Czechs bounced back in their second-round qualifying tie following Learner Tien's straight-sets win over Jakub Mensik in the opening singles rubber.

The USA are record 32-time winners of the competition but have not lifted the trophy since 2007.

Christian Harrison and Austin Krajicek are set to take on Czech pair Adam Pavlasek and Patrik Rikl in Saturday's doubles, with Shelton due to play Mensik before Lehecka faces Tien in the reverse singles.

South Korea seized a 2-0 lead over India in Seoul as Kwon Soon-woo and Chung Hyeon both staged dramatic comebacks.

Kwon recovered to beat 367th-ranked Dhakshineswar Suresh 3-6, 6-3, 6-4. Chung, a former Australian Open semi-finalist whose career has been derailed by injuries, also came from a set down to overcome Sumit Nagal, 2-6, 6-4, 7-5.

"I felt a lot more nervous than I have in a long time," Kwon said.

"Of course, I usually feel some nerves, but today they were particularly intense. At the beginning, my vision was almost blurred. From the second set onward, I began to feel more relaxed."

Austria are Belgium all locked at 1-1 in Vienna.

Jurij Rodionov beat Gauthier Onclin in straight sets to put Austria ahead, but Zizou Bergs fought back to see off Lukas Neumayer 2-6, 6-4, 6-2.

Canada are hosting France in Quebec City, with three other ties starting on Saturday.

Newly-crowned US Open champion Alexander Zverev makes a quick return to action for Germany, who must get past Croatia in Halle in their quest for a first Davis Cup crown since 1993.

Spain continue their tilt at a seventh title against Chile in Santiago, while Britain, featuring surprise Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery, welcome Ecuador to London.

The seven winners this weekend will join hosts and three-time defending champions Italy in Bologna in November's eight-team Finals.

articles.title: Dennis Allen's message to Bears defense before Week 2 vs. Vikings
articles.summary: Bears defensive coordinator shared his message for the defense heading into a pivotal Week 2 game vs. the Vikings.
articles.body:
There has been a lot of talk about how well the Chicago Bears offense performed in the season opener, but there were also concerns with how the defense allowed the Carolina Panthers to score 37 points. That is the most the Bears have allowed in an opener since 2023.

Despite the struggles from Chicago's defense in the season opener, defensive coordinator Dennis Allen is looking ahead to the Bears' Week 2 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings , which will also serve as their first NFC North game of the season.

"I mean, line up again. Let's go. Week 2," Allen said. "Like, we have to be man enough to admit and see where we fell short, all right? What can we do to improve our performance? What can we do to maybe improve our preparation, those types of things? And then let's focus on playing outstanding this week, because that one's done. Let's move on to this one and let's play better as a group."

Photos from Bears' historic 59-37 win over Panthers in Week 1

Minnesota is coming off a strong opener of their own. They were the only NFC North team to hold their opponent to under 30 points after shutting the Green Bay Packers out in the fourth quarter and putting up 29 unanswered points to win 39-22 after being down 22-10 late in the third quarter. Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson also had quite the opener with 92 receiving yards and two touchdowns.

Chicago has not done well against the Vikings in the past few years, only winning two of their last 10 matchups against Minnesota. However, one of those wins was last year in head coach Ben Johnson's first season, and he has turned the Bears into a much more competitive team in the division.

Furthermore, in the 130 times Chicago has played against the Vikings, the Bears have won 18 out of 19 games where they scored at least 30 points. With Johnson's offense, Chicago is certainly capable of putting up that many points.

articles.title: Nick Saban thinks there's 'absolutely nothing wrong' with Sam Leavitt for Ole Miss vs LSU
articles.summary: Nick Saban doesn't believe Sam Leavitt, currently on LSU's injury report for its game against Ole Miss, is actually injured.
articles.body:
Sam Leavitt was listed on LSU 's injury report this week in the latest of many twists and turns surrounding Lane Kiffin's return vs Ole Miss football in Oxford on Sept. 19 (6:30 p.m., ABC).

Add Nick Saban to the list of those who doubt Leavitt is injured.

"If I was a betting man, I would say there's absolutely nothing wrong with Sam Leavitt ," Saban said on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Sept. 18. "So, I would be psychologically telling the defensive players that this doesn't matter. 'Sam Leavitt is going to play, he's going to be the best, we've got to stop him. Don't lose your edge because you think he's not going to play.' And then he shows up and plays, and it's a downer."

Saban will be in Oxford on Sept. 19 as part of ESPN's "College GameDay" crew. Actor Morgan Shepherd , a huge Rebels fan, will be the guest picker.

LSU's star quarterback was upgraded from doubtful to questionable on Sept. 17, and there will be two more injury reports released before No. 9 Ole Miss (2-0) faces the No. 7 Tigers (2-0). One will be released on the evening of Sept. 18 and another 90 minutes before kickoff.

Lane Kiffin roast before Ole Miss-LSU at The Lyric in Oxford, MS. See our best photos

Leavitt didn't appear hurt in LSU's victory over Louisiana Tech on Sept. 12, and Kiffin hasn't addressed it. There have been media reports that Leavitt is dealing with a shoulder issue.

Some believe Leavitt's placement on LSU's injury report is a mind game from Kiffin before his highly anticipated return to Ole Miss . Kiffin went 55-19 with the Rebels from 2020-25 and left for LSU right before Ole Miss entered the 2025 College Football Playoff.

The SEC defines a questionable designation as a player being "uncertain to play" or having a 50% chance to play. The conference's reporting policy states that acts "intended to hide a student-athlete's true participation status for competitive or strategic reasons" or acts that can reasonably be interpreted as "misleading" aren't allowed.

The SEC also says schools should take extra measures to act in good faith when disclosing the status of notable players, such as starting quarterbacks. Penalties for inaccurate reports range from $25,000 to $100,000 in football and can include "accountability measures" for head coaches. SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey can administer penalties based on the circumstances.

Leavitt has passed for 574 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions while rushing for 135 yards and five touchdowns. He'll compete in a high-profile quarterback matchup with the Rebels' Trinidad Chambliss — who's passed for 561 yards, five touchdowns and one interception — if he plays.

articles.title: Brewers Magic Number: What Needs To Happen To Lock Up Bye, No. 1 Seed?
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers enter play on Friday with the best record in baseball
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers enter play on Friday with the best record in baseball, and even though they have already won the National League Central, there is still plenty to play for.

If there was any doubt about whether the Brewers would keep their foot on the gas, fans need to look no further than the game right after their division championship celebration. There was no hangover lineup for Pat Murphy and he used his best relievers to get the win. The Brewers are trying to secure a first-round bye and home-field advantage, with the Los Angeles Dodgers on their tail.

The Brewers are two games clear of the Dodgers for the No. 1 seed, and six games clear of the Atlanta Braves . With nine games left to play, not much has to happen to secure a bye.

Any combination of Brewers wins and Braves losses equaling four would lock up a bye for the Brewers. If the Brewers win the first two games of their series against the Baltimore Orioles and the Braves lose to the Houston Astros on Friday and Saturday, the Brewers will have locked up a bye by the time games start on Sunday. Then they would only be playing for seeding, but they want the No. 1 seed.

The Brewers and Dodgers are both trying to lock up the top seed in the National League, but the Brewers have been in the driver's seat for most of the year. The Brewers have series remaining against the Orioles, Philadelphia Phillies and St. Louis Cardinals .

Meanwhile, the Dodgers will play the San Francisco Giants at home, the San Diego Padres and then the Giants again, but on the road. In the next nine games, the Brewers need to have any combination of wins and Dodgers losses totaling seven to clinch.

The Brewers own the season series against the Dodgers, so another way of looking at it is to say that the Brewers need to at least finish with the same record as the Dodgers, and they will have home-field advantage in the National League postseason.

articles.title: Miami football news: Malachi Toney reveals cold 'hunter' mentality
articles.summary: Malachi Toney isn’t interested in being chased. The Miami superstar wide receiver made his mentality perfectly clear as the Hurricanes continue their pursuit...
articles.body:
Malachi Toney isn't interested in being chased.

The Miami superstar wide receiver made his mentality perfectly clear as the Hurricanes continue their pursuit of a national championship.

"I ain't the hunted. I am the hunter," Toney said, via The Journal Media.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

That mentality extends well beyond individual success. Toney also made it clear that if he leaves Miami without winning a national championship, he'll consider his college career a failure.

That's an enormous standard, but Toney has already established himself as one of the most electric playmakers in college football. After setting Miami's single-season record with 109 receptions as a true freshman, the 5-foot-11 receiver has somehow become even more dangerous as a sophomore. Toney enters Friday night's matchup against Wake Forest with 16 receptions for 330 yards and four touchdowns through only two games.

His combination of quickness, route-running, and explosiveness makes him a nightmare in one-on-one coverage. Toney opened the season by torching Stanford for 234 yards and three touchdowns before adding 96 yards and another score against Florida A&M despite playing limited snaps in Miami's blowout victory .

Now comes another opportunity under the national spotlight. No. 5 Miami travels to undefeated Wake Forest on Friday night looking to improve to 3-0, and another monster performance would only strengthen Toney's early case as one of the players to watch in the Heisman Trophy race.

Individual awards aren't what Toney ultimately wants, though. He's hunting something considerably bigger.

And anything short of a championship apparently won't satisfy him.

Wake Forest hosts Miami for a massive contest on Friday night on ESPN. This one could be a thriller!

articles.title: Néstor Lorenzo empieza la renovación: Los 13 ausentes del Mundial para empezar una nueva era
articles.standfirst: Cambio de ciclo en la Selección Colombia: Néstor Lorenzo hace varios cambios en la lista con respecto al Mundial
articles.summary: Cambio de ciclo en la Selección Colombia: Néstor Lorenzo hace varios cambios en la lista con respecto al Mundial
articles.body: El director técnico de la Selección Colombia de Mayores, Néstor Lorenzo, dio a conocer la lista de 26 convocados para los próximos partidos amistosos de finales de septiembre y comienzos de octubre de 2026. La convocatoria marca el inicio de una profunda reestructuración en el combinado nacional con miras al ciclo mundialista de 2030, caracterizada por la llegada de múltiples caras nuevas y la ausencia de varios referentes habituales. El objetivo del director técnico con esta lista en la que figuran numerosos ausentes con respecto al mundial, es la de probar nuevas caras de cara a la renovación que tiene que acometer la Selección para el próximo ciclo. Esto no significa que varios de los ausentes estén en este nuevo proceso, pero el profesor matizó que quiere dar oportunidad a otros jugadores para demostrar su valía en estos amistosos: "Hay que darle rodaje a los jugadores, hay jugadores que tienen mucho talento", señaló en la rueda de prensa. Esta entrega se convirtió en la primera convocatoria tras las renuncias de James Rodríguez y Juan Fernando Quintero al equipo nacional. A estas ausencias se sumaron las de futbolistas habituales en las últimas citas internacionales, entre los que destacan: La baja de Luis Díaz representa una de las novedades más comentadas. No obstante, su ausencia responde a un acuerdo previo entre el cuerpo técnico y el jugador para brindarle descanso, tras conversaciones directas entre el extremo guajiro y el seleccionador. Néstor Lorenzo apostó por nombres emergentes y jugadores del torneo local e internacional para afrontar el inicio de este nuevo proceso. Entre los citados se encuentran futbolistas como Roger Caicedo, Matías Orozco, Daniel Arcila, Samuel Velásquez, Camilo Durán y Juan Manuel Rengifo, acompañados por elementos con mayor recorrido en el proceso como Daniel Muñoz, Dávinson Sánchez, Jhon Arias y Yáser Asprilla. "Hay que darle rodaje a nuevos jugadores para que la camiseta no les pese. Y que lo que hacen en sus equipos lo hagan en la selección. De pronto hay chicos que tienen mucho talento y prefieren jugar más liberados de esa presión", es el objetivo de Néstor Lorenzo con esta lista de jugadores que tendrán la oportunidad de marcar la renovación de Colombia.

articles.title: Asian Games: Karate team leaves without coaches; equestrian riders caught in accred maze
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: India’s karate team is heading to the Asiad without a dedicated coach while five equestrian riders in Tokyo are scrambling to get accredita.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s karate team is heading to the Asiad without a dedicated coach while five equestrian riders in Tokyo are scrambling to get accreditation for their personal coaches. Some are even considering a two-hour train journey to Nagoya to sort out the issue in person, TOI has learnt.For the karate contingent, reigning Asian champion Alisha Choudhary’s repeated pleas to sports authorities and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) officials for accreditation for her coach, Vikas Panchal, have gone unheard. The two-member team also includes Chetan Bhatt (men’s kumite 84kg), with Adikessava Peroumal Sinouvassane the designated ‘team leader’.When the sports ministry’s sanction clearing coaches was issued on September 2, no coach was named for karate. Alisha has since sent multiple emails and reminders, underlining that Panchal has trained her for 11 years and guided her to every major international achievement, including her historic gold at the 2026 Asian Karate Championship. He is certified by the World Karate Federation and Asian Karate Federation and has accompanied her to international camps and competitions.Interestingly, during a bout, only a coach can occupy the coaching corner and seek a video review by throwing the challenge block onto the mat. The team leader cannot perform those duties, leaving India’s karate athletes without vital technical and tactical support.The equestrian camp, meanwhile, is caught in its own accreditation scramble. All five foreign coaches are awaiting accreditation and, without it, cannot enter the competition or training venue. The riders are coordinating by phone with IOA contingent staff based in Aichi and Nagoya, a logistical headache made worse by the distance between the two locations.Some riders are now contemplating a roughly two-hour train journey from Tokyo to Nagoya simply to meet IOA officials and get their coaches’ accreditations sorted, potentially losing an entire day of crucial training.It is learnt the five coaches were approved late by the IOA and sports authorities, despite the rider-horse combinations and coaches’ names having been shared with the IOA in May. The riders had also been following up on travel approvals.None of these five coaches are govt funded. Their entire Games expenses will be borne by the riders themselves. Yet, they are still struggling for the accreditation needed to do the job. The accreditation troubles come on top of the equestrian contingent scrambling for hay, bedding and fodder for their horses, with the IOA-appointed ad-hoc committee citing a “shortage of govt funds”.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England fast bowler Carse to face no charges over alleged nightclub assault
articles.summary: Derbyshire Police said they were investigating an alleged assault but have now decided no further action will be taken.
articles.body:
England fast bowler Brydon Carse will face no charges after an investigation into an alleged assault was closed by Derbyshire Police, the force has said.

But the 31-year-old remains subject to a separate probe by the Cricket Regulator, the disciplinary arm of the English game, who will assess if he has a case to answer under their regulations.

Carse was handcuffed by officers after a celebratory night out with Durham teammates on August 23 in Derby, central England, and it was later confirmed he had been arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly, before being “de-arrested” after agreeing to depart.

Derbyshire Police said they were investigating an alleged assault in connection with the incident but have now decided no further action will be taken.

In a statement on Friday, the force said: “An investigation into reports of an assault in Derby city centre has been closed.

“Officers attended Molly Malones in the Wardwick, Derby, in the early hours of Sunday 23 August. A man was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly and was then de-arrested after his details were taken by officers.”

Subsequent enquiries were made pursuing the allegations of an assault but, after the alleged victim was identified and spoken to, no further action was taken, police said.

Videos of Carse’s arrest were released on social media, with Carse seen talking to Durham teammate Matthew Potts, while former England captain Ben Stokes – who also plays for northeast county Durham – was pictured in the background.

Carse, who has taken 58 wickets in 14 Tests at a shade more than 30 apiece, has continued playing for Durham since the episode took place, helping the side win the Second Division title in the first-class County Championship.

Carse was immediately removed from the squad before the second Test against Pakistan, then left out of the final match too, having not been selected on cricketing grounds for the opening encounter of a series where England whitewashed the tourists 3-0.

While officially available for selection for the ongoing white-ball series against Sri Lanka, he was again omitted.

England’s limited-overs head coach Brendon McCullum, speaking earlier this week, reminded his side of their off-field responsibilities, adding: “I’ve spoken to Carsey a lot and it’s the same message – you need to make good decisions off the field that allow you to be able to be the best version of yourself.

“As far as Carsey is concerned, it’s a good chance for him now to get his house in order and then push for selection for the next opportunity that arises.”

Carse’s arrest was the latest in a series of alcohol-fuelled controversies that have dogged England since their disastrous tour of New Zealand and Australia at the end of last year.

Test captain Joe Root, speaking before the Lord’s Test, said he was “hacked off” by the growing list of drink-related incidents involving England cricketers.

Turning to Carse, he said, “I don’t think I’m speaking out of turn in saying he’s very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I’m sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself.”

articles.title: Kirill Marchenko Addresses Blue Jackets Future Amid NHL Trade Rumors After Agent's Comments
articles.summary: The Columbus Blue Jackets might have to continue dealing with more trade rumors amid the team's ongoing contract dispute with Adam Fantilli.
articles.body:
The Columbus Blue Jackets might have to continue dealing with more trade rumors amid the team's ongoing contract dispute with Adam Fantilli.

Jackets winger Kirill Marchenko did not answer definitively when asked Friday if he enjoyed playing in Columbus.

When asked if he "liked playing hockey here," Marchenko answered, "Yeah, I love to play hockey."

Marchenko was then asked to clarify on whether that applied "here."

"It's a good question," Marchenko said (around 3:20 mark in video). "I can say yes, because I play here for sure. But... I can answer only on the hockey."

Marchenko, a native Russian speaker , also noted he was not conducting the interview in his first language.

His agent told reporters earlier this offseason Marchenko does not intend to re-sign with the Blue Jackets, per The Athletic's Aaron Portzline .

Marchenko is currently signed through the upcoming season and set to hit restricted free agency in 2027, per PuckPedia . He is set to play his age-25 season under a $3.85 million cap hit.

The winger recorded 67 points, including a team-high 27 goals, in 76 games for the Blue Jackets last season while mostly playing alongside Fantilli.

Blue Jackets general manager Don Waddell told reporters Wednesday he met recently with Marchenko, who told Waddell he's "not sure what's going to happen" when he hits restricted free agency.

"He said, 'I'm going to play my butt off here, and help this team win,'" Waddell said. "He's really a good person that cares."

Marchenko's comments come after Fantilli, a pending restricted free agent, refused to report to training camp amid ongoing negotiations for a new deal.

Waddell said at his Wednesday press conference he is "still confident" the Blue Jackets will be able to finalize a new deal with Fantilli "in the near future."

This isn't the first contract negotiation that has become a drawn-out process this offseason in Columbus, where the Jackets finalized a three-year extension for starting netminder Jet Greaves just before a scheduled arbitration hearing in July.

The Blue Jackets have also previously dealt with trade rumors surrounding reigning Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski, who vetoed a deal that would have sent him to the Dallas Stars in June.

Werenski, who has two years remaining on his own contract, said earlier this month he will "hopefully" sign an extension in Columbus when he becomes eligible next summer.

The Blue Jackets missed the playoffs for a sixth straight year last season after ranking 19th in the NHL with three goals per game. Keeping last season's top two goalscorers in Marchenko and Fantilli in the fold could be key to Columbus' hopes of putting together a more competitive campaign this fall.

articles.title: Do the Clippers Have a Better Future Than They're Given Credit for?
articles.summary: ESPN's new three-year outlook buried the Clippers, and even the people who built the ranking admit the roster is better than the number.
articles.body:
Being ranked 23rd out of 30 usually means a team is bad, and that is exactly what makes the Los Angeles Clippers ' spot in ESPN's new future power rankings so strange, because nobody involved seems to think the actual basketball team is bad at all.

The Clippers sat fifth in this same exercise a year ago.

Twelve months and one league investigation later, they have fallen 18 spots, and the reason has almost nothing to do with the players.

"The Clippers ranked a half-dozen spots higher before the NBA handed down a draconian punishment for cap circumvention," Zach Kram wrote in the three-year outlook published this week .

Kram added that the roster is more talented than many of the teams ranked around it, and that the management, draft and market scores are what took the hit.

The league stripped five first-round picks, fined the team $30 million and suspended owner Steve Ballmer for a year, with Bobby Marks noting that Lawrence Frank's six-month suspension carries past the February trade deadline and that a team with no picks to trade could sit in a holding position until next summer.

The projected group of point guard Darius Garland, guard Kris Dunn, forward Brandon Ingram, forward Rui Hachimura and center Brook Lopez, with guard Bradley Beal behind them, is a real rotation, and there are honest arguments this team stays competitive right now.

ESPN notes the franchise has put together 15 straight winning seasons, the longest active run in the league, and a group this deep could outplay outside expectations again this year.

Toronto's 2031 and 2033 first-round picks and a 2027 swap right came back in the trade that sent forward Kawhi Leonard north, so the cupboard is not completely empty either, and that is not nothing for a franchise that was supposed to be starting from zero.

The answer to the headline question is yes for this season and probably no for the two after it.

A future power ranking is not a prediction of this year's standings, and judged strictly on the next 12 months, 23rd is silly for a team with this much usable talent.

Judged on three years, the ranking is doing its job, because the missing drafts are real, the front office is hamstrung, and one of ESPN's writers even predicts the long winning-season streak finally breaks before the window closes.

The fair read is that the Clippers are underrated for this season and rated about right on the long view, since the question of whether the championship window shut was answered the day the picks left.

Winning now was never optional in Los Angeles anyway, because a team with no picks cannot even run a proper rebuild, and every competitive season from here makes the eventual reset shallower.

Rankings measure risk, and the risk is real, but the games still get played by the players, and the players here are good.

Good team, cloudy future, and both things are true at once.

articles.title: Eli Manning Admits Arch Manning's Start Against Ohio State Made Him “Nervous” as He Shares Honest Feelings on Texas QB
articles.summary: You would think two Super Bowl rings and a career built on fourth-quarter comebacks would make Eli Manning immune to late-game stress. But as Ohio State and...
articles.body:
You would think two Super Bowl rings and a career built on fourth-quarter comebacks would make Eli Manning immune to late-game stress. But as Ohio State and Texas traded blows in a nail-biting epic on September 12, even the NFL legend was sweating every snap. Eli Manning admitted to feeling a rush of emotions while watching his nephew, Texas Longhorns QB Arch Manning , battle through a difficult first-half performance against the Buckeyes.

"I want him to play so well," Eli Manning said on the Colin Cowherd podcast on September 17 when asked about how he feels when he sees Arch play. "I see how hard he works and how committed he is and everything he puts into this. So I want him to play well. I want him to win. I was nervous. I was quiet in that first half. It was such a weird start to the game."

Texas had a sluggish start against the Buckeyes. The Longhorns fell into a 20-3 deficit heading into the fourth quarter. Not all of the offensive issues were on Arch. Texas RB Raleek Brown fumbled the ball on the first play. Ohio State went on to score a field goal.

During the Longhorns' following drive, Arch Manning looked to have connected with Cam Coleman on a deep pass. But the Auburn transfer couldn't hold on to the catch. The ball bounced off Coleman, and Ohio State CB Jaylen McClain converted it into an interception. However, Arch Manning also struggled to access the middle of the field in the first half.

The struggles continued to start the second half. Even during the comeback, Texas had to convert two critical fourth downs to keep their drives going. However, by then, Arch Manning looked to have a grip on the game. Eli Manning was thrilled by Arch's response to adversity. His calm demeanor allowed the sophomore to engineer three consecutive scoring drives in the fourth quarter.

"He stayed patient even early in that second half. They weren't giving him anything. He didn't have some shots. He missed a throw. He didn't force anything down the field. He stayed patient and waited until they got the right calls. Got guys open, and then had three great drives to go win that thing. So I was fired up for him. I was celebrating that night alongside with him from New Jersey," Eli Manning added .

By guiding the Longhorns to victory, Manning became the first-ever Texas quarterback to defeat three top-10 opponents at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. He also remains a perfect 10-0 as a starter at home. After the victory, even Eli became a part of the celebration and texted Arch a simple message, "Way to stay patient."

Arch Manning's relationship with Eli Manning is built on a tight-knit family bond. Eli operates less like a critical coach and more like a protective mentor and supportive uncle for the Texas QB. When Arch needs help navigating his football career, he splits his questions strategically between his uncles.

Peyton Manning is his go-to resource for on-field X's and O's. If Arch asks Peyton about a two-minute drill or a defensive scheme, Peyton will famously leave him seven-minute-long, highly dense voice memos breaking down the tape.

Eli Manning, on the other hand, is his person when it comes to handling the psychological weight of stardom. Arch leans heavily on Eli to learn how to deal with New York-style media scrutiny, public expectations, and managing the immense pressure that comes with carrying the "Manning" surname. Eli has publicly praised Arch's grounding, noting that he is a "sponge" who leads with humility rather than buying into his own hype.

The former Giants QB has even jokingly shared practical "uncle advice" with Arch, such as implementing a strict "team rule" to never take fan photos anywhere and serving alcohol to avoid easy media traps.

articles.body:
Chelsea have made their first attacking changes of the game – and it's bad news for their Brazilian wonderkid Estevao .

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

Chelsea are 1-0 down against Brentford , and with 70 minutes on the clock, Xabi Alonso has had to make his move to try and change the game back in his team's favour.

The new manager has opted to bring off striker Danny Welbeck and move Morgan Rogers up front. Geovany Quenda has come on in Rogers' usual position on the left.

That's bad news for Estevao Willian. There was already concern that he's not starting in the league. Now he seems to have slipped further back in the pecking order.

Tactical concerns all part of Alonso's Estevao decision

Estevao (Photo by Brendon Thorne/Getty Images)

Now of course there's more to it than just a hierarchy – Quenda is playing on the left, while Estevao wants to play on the right or centrally. And given we're not going to take off Cole Palmer , that would either mean Palmer or Estevao playing on the left where they aren't really at their best.

We're sure Estevao will be the next man on – but still, the fact he's not even first sub anymore is not great for him. His frustrating will only be growing watching Pedro Neto toil on the right flank for 90 minutes.

Jordan Henderson was the outstanding Chelsea player in the first half, not for doing anything flashy but just for giving this team some calm and control in midfield.

Henderson is making his debut tonight, a big moment for him and for Chelsea as they try to figure out their midfield depth chart.
